candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: UKNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United Kingdom. Also called UK charity type, British non-profit category, UK voluntary sector classification. Examples: a registered charity, a community interest company (CIC), a benevolent society.

candidates.label: USNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United States. Also called US charity type, American non-profit category, US voluntary sector classification. Examples: a 501(c)(3) organization, a public charity, a private foundation.

candidates.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
candidates.comment: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings is a place representing an important historical landmark or building. Also called historical site, heritage building, monument. Examples: Eiffel Tower, Colosseum, Statue of Liberty, a historic courthouse.

candidates.label: Impact
candidates.comment: The effect or influence of one thing on another.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: Characteristic
candidates.comment: A distinguishing quality or feature of something.

candidates.label: EventStatusType
candidates.comment: An EventStatusType is a StatusEnumeration whose instances represent various states an Event may be in. Also called event state, status of event. Examples: EventScheduled, EventCancelled, EventPostponed, EventRescheduled.

types.embedding_query_text: VehicleType: A category or class of vehicles. Also called Car Type, Automobile Class. Examples: black SUVs, trucks.

chosen_type.label: Class
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'VehicleType' is a classification or category, which directly matches schema.org/Class.

candidates.label: CarUsageType
candidates.comment: An enumeration indicating a specific purpose or usage of a car. Also called vehicle use category, automobile purpose, car application type. Examples: Commercial rental, driving school, taxi service, personal use.

candidates.label: Car
candidates.comment: A wheeled, self-powered motor vehicle primarily used for personal transportation. Also called automobile, motorcar, auto, vehicle. Examples: Toyota Camry, Ford F-150, Tesla Model 3, Honda Civic.

candidates.label: Class
candidates.comment: An intangible concept representing a category or type of entity, equivalent to rdfs:Class. Also called type, category, kind, schema. Examples: "Person" class, "Product" class, "Event" class. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a specific term within a vocabulary.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: MapCategoryType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of different categories or kinds of maps. Also called map type, map classification, cartography category. Examples: "RoadMap", "SatelliteMap", "TerrainMap", "HybridMap".

candidates.label: Motorcycle
candidates.comment: A vehicle that is a single-track, two-wheeled motor vehicle. Also called motorbike, two-wheeler, scooter. Examples: a Harley-Davidson, a Honda CBR, a Vespa scooter. Distinct from MotorizedBicycle, which is primarily a bicycle with an assisting motor.

candidates.label: AutoDealer
candidates.comment: An AutoDealer is an AutomotiveBusiness that sells new or used vehicles. Also called car dealership, vehicle retailer, auto sales. Examples: a Ford dealership, a used car lot, a luxury car showroom. Distinct from AutoRental, which rents vehicles rather than selling them.

candidates.label: MeasurementTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common types or dimensions of measurements. Also called dimension type, measurement category, sizing parameter. Examples: "chest circumference", "inseam length", "screw gauge", "wheel diameter".

candidates.label: EngineSpecification
candidates.comment: An EngineSpecification is a StructuredValue providing details about a vehicle's engine. Also called engine details, motor specs, powertrain information. Examples: Engine type (e.g., V6), displacement (e.g., 2.0L), horsepower, fuel type.

candidates.label: AutoRental
candidates.comment: An AutoRental is an AutomotiveBusiness that provides vehicles for temporary hire. Also called car hire, vehicle rental agency, rent-a-car. Examples: Hertz, Enterprise Rent-A-Car, a local van rental service. Distinct from AutoDealer, which sells vehicles.

types.embedding_query_text: Structure: A building or other object constructed from several parts. Also called Construction, Edifice, Building. Examples: white canopy tent, large white canopy tent.

chosen_type.label: Structure
chosen_type.definition: A building or other object constructed from several parts.
chosen_type.justification: No existing type directly captures the general concept of a constructed 'structure' that isn't necessarily a building or civic. 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: GovernmentBuilding
candidates.comment: A GovernmentBuilding is a civic structure that houses government operations or services. Also called public building, state edifice, official premises. Examples: city hall, parliament building, courthouse, post office. Distinct from GovernmentOffice, which is a specific type of organization within a government building.

candidates.label: PlaceOfWorship
candidates.comment: A PlaceOfWorship is a civic structure or building used for religious services and spiritual activities. Also called religious building, house of worship, sanctuary. Examples: a church, a synagogue, a mosque, a temple. Distinct from Museum, which is for exhibiting artifacts.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

candidates.label: LegislativeBuilding
candidates.comment: A LegislativeBuilding is a government building civic structure where legislative bodies meet and conduct their work. Also called capitol building, parliament house, assembly hall. Examples: the U.S. Capitol, a state capitol building, the Houses of Parliament. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: AnatomicalStructure
candidates.comment: An AnatomicalStructure is a MedicalEntity representing any part of the human body, such as organs, tissues, or cells. Also called body part, biological structure, anatomical component. Examples: The heart, a bone, a muscle, a neuron, the liver. Distinct from AnatomicalSystem, which is a group of structures working together.

candidates.label: House
candidates.comment: A House is an accommodation type representing a building or structure intended for human or other creature habitation. Also called dwelling, residence, home. Examples: a single-family home, a townhouse, a cottage. Distinct from Apartment, which is a unit within a larger building, and HotelRoom, which is a temporary lodging unit.

candidates.label: Room
candidates.comment: A distinguishable space within a structure, typically separated by interior walls. Also called chamber, compartment, space, area. Examples: a hotel room, a living room, a bedroom, a conference room.

candidates.label: Joint
candidates.comment: A Joint is an anatomical structure where two or more bones make contact, facilitating movement or providing stability. Also called articulation, bone joint, anatomical junction. Examples: knee joint, elbow joint, hip joint, shoulder joint. Distinct from Bone, which is a single skeletal component.

candidates.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
candidates.comment: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings is a place representing an important historical landmark or building. Also called historical site, heritage building, monument. Examples: Eiffel Tower, Colosseum, Statue of Liberty, a historic courthouse.

types.embedding_query_text: Equipment: The necessary items for a particular purpose. Also called Gear, Apparatus, Tools. Examples: forklifts.

chosen_type.label: HowToTool
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/HowToTool explicitly includes 'equipment' in its 'Also called' list and fits the definition of necessary items for a purpose.

candidates.label: HowToTool
candidates.comment: A HowToTool is a HowToItem that is used but not consumed when performing the instructions for how to achieve a result. Also called instrument, utensil, equipment. Examples: a screwdriver, a mixing bowl, a hammer, a computer. Distinct from HowToSupply, which is consumed during the process.

candidates.label: MedicalDevicePurpose
candidates.comment: An enumeration of categories for medical devices, organized by their purpose or intended use. Also called device use, medical equipment function, intended purpose. Examples: "Diagnostic", "Therapeutic", "Surgical", "Monitoring".

candidates.label: HowToItem
candidates.comment: A HowToItem is a list item used as either a tool or supply when following instructions in a HowTo guide. Also called instruction component, how-to resource, procedural element. Examples: a screwdriver, flour, a measuring cup, a specific software application.

candidates.label: MedicalDevice
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any object used in a medical capacity for diagnosing or treating a patient. Also called medical instrument, healthcare apparatus, diagnostic tool. Examples: a stethoscope, an MRI machine, a surgical scalpel, a blood pressure monitor.

candidates.label: UseAction
candidates.comment: The act of applying an object to its intended purpose or function. Also called utilize, employ, operate. Examples: using a tool to fix something, consuming food, wearing clothes.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: HowToSupply
candidates.comment: A HowToSupply is a HowToItem that is consumed or used up when performing the instructions for how to achieve a result. Also called consumable item, ingredient, material. Examples: flour, sugar, paint, batteries. Distinct from HowToTool, which is used but not consumed.

candidates.label: FireStation
candidates.comment: A FireStation is a CivicStructure housing firemen and fire-fighting equipment. Also called fire department, firehouse. Examples: The local city fire station, a volunteer fire department, a regional fire and rescue service.

candidates.label: SportingGoodsStore
candidates.comment: A retail store specializing in the sale of equipment and apparel for sports and outdoor activities. Also called sports shop, athletic store, outdoor gear retailer. Examples: 'Dick's Sporting Goods', 'REI', 'Decathlon'.

candidates.label: CarUsageType
candidates.comment: An enumeration indicating a specific purpose or usage of a car. Also called vehicle use category, automobile purpose, car application type. Examples: Commercial rental, driving school, taxi service, personal use.

types.embedding_query_text: Container: An object used for holding or transporting something. Also called Receptacle, Holder, Crate. Examples: cardboard boxes.

chosen_type.label: Container
chosen_type.definition: An object used for holding or transporting something.
chosen_type.justification: No existing type directly captures the general concept of a container. 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: TransferAction
candidates.comment: The act of moving an object, whether animate or inanimate, from one location to another. Also called move, transport, relocate. Examples: transferring funds between bank accounts, moving furniture to a new house, transferring a patient to another hospital.

candidates.label: SelfStorage
candidates.comment: A local business providing rental units for individuals and businesses to store their belongings. Also called storage facility, mini-storage, public storage. Examples: 'U-Haul Self-Storage', 'Extra Space Storage', 'Local Storage Units'.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: DeliveryMethod
candidates.comment: An enumeration describing a standardized procedure for transferring a product or service to a customer's chosen destination. Also called Shipping method, fulfillment method, delivery option, shipping carrier. Examples: Mail, freight, direct download, in-store pickup, UPS, FedEx. Distinct from DeliveryChargeSpecification, which specifies the cost of a delivery method.

candidates.label: ParcelDelivery
candidates.comment: A ParcelDelivery is an intangible entity representing the delivery of a parcel via postal or commercial service. Also called package delivery, shipment, courier service. Examples: a UPS package delivery, a letter sent via postal service, an Amazon shipment. Distinct from Order, which is the transaction itself.

candidates.label: ReceiveAction
candidates.comment: ReceiveAction is a TransferAction representing the act of physically or electronically taking delivery of an object that has been transferred. Also called accepting delivery, getting, obtaining. Examples: receiving a package, getting an email, accepting a file download, taking delivery of a new car. Distinct from SendAction, which is the reciprocal action; Distinct from TakeAction, which implies ownership transfer.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: HowToItem
candidates.comment: A HowToItem is a list item used as either a tool or supply when following instructions in a HowTo guide. Also called instruction component, how-to resource, procedural element. Examples: a screwdriver, flour, a measuring cup, a specific software application.

candidates.label: FulfillmentTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: A FulfillmentTypeEnumeration is an Enumeration representing different ways a product can be fulfilled or delivered. Also called delivery method, order fulfillment type, shipping option. Examples: Delivery, Pickup, InStorePickup, CurbsidePickup.

types.embedding_query_text: Vehicle: A means of transport, especially on land. Also called Car, Automobile, Transport. Examples: van.

chosen_type.label: Vehicle
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Vehicle' directly matches schema.org/Vehicle, a device used for transporting people or cargo.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: Car
candidates.comment: A wheeled, self-powered motor vehicle primarily used for personal transportation. Also called automobile, motorcar, auto, vehicle. Examples: Toyota Camry, Ford F-150, Tesla Model 3, Honda Civic.

candidates.label: TravelAction
candidates.comment: The act of moving from a starting location to a destination using a specified mode of transport. Also called journey, commute, voyage. Examples: traveling by car from home to work, flying from New York to London, taking a bus to another city.

candidates.label: CarUsageType
candidates.comment: An enumeration indicating a specific purpose or usage of a car. Also called vehicle use category, automobile purpose, car application type. Examples: Commercial rental, driving school, taxi service, personal use.

candidates.label: AutoRental
candidates.comment: An AutoRental is an AutomotiveBusiness that provides vehicles for temporary hire. Also called car hire, vehicle rental agency, rent-a-car. Examples: Hertz, Enterprise Rent-A-Car, a local van rental service. Distinct from AutoDealer, which sells vehicles.

candidates.label: TransferAction
candidates.comment: The act of moving an object, whether animate or inanimate, from one location to another. Also called move, transport, relocate. Examples: transferring funds between bank accounts, moving furniture to a new house, transferring a patient to another hospital.

candidates.label: BusOrCoach
candidates.comment: A BusOrCoach is a Vehicle designed to carry multiple passengers, with coaches being luxury versions for long-distance travel. Also called omnibus, motorcoach, passenger bus, tour bus. Examples: city bus, Greyhound coach, school bus, double-decker bus.

candidates.label: Motorcycle
candidates.comment: A vehicle that is a single-track, two-wheeled motor vehicle. Also called motorbike, two-wheeler, scooter. Examples: a Harley-Davidson, a Honda CBR, a Vespa scooter. Distinct from MotorizedBicycle, which is primarily a bicycle with an assisting motor.

candidates.label: TaxiService
candidates.comment: A local business or service offering vehicles for hire with drivers for local transportation, typically charging based on distance. Also called cab company, taxi provider, ride-hailing service. Examples: 'Yellow Cab Co.', 'Uber', 'Lyft', a local taxi firm. Distinct from Taxi, which refers to an instance of the service or the vehicle itself.

candidates.label: AutomotiveBusiness
candidates.comment: A LocalBusiness focused on vehicle-related services like repair, sales, or parts. Also called car business, auto service center, vehicle dealership. Examples: "Joe's Auto Repair", "Luxury Car Sales", "Parts 'R' Us". Distinct from AutoWash, which specifically cleans vehicles.

types.embedding_query_text: Barrier: A fence or other obstacle that prevents movement or access. Also called Obstacle, Blockade, Fence. Examples: metal barricade.

chosen_type.label: Barrier
chosen_type.definition: An obstacle that prevents movement or access.
chosen_type.justification: No existing type directly captures the concept of a barrier or obstacle. 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: Bridge
candidates.comment: A Bridge is a CivicStructure built to span physical obstacles like water, valleys, or roads, facilitating passage. Also called overpass, viaduct, span. Examples: Golden Gate Bridge, Brooklyn Bridge, a pedestrian bridge.

candidates.label: Joint
candidates.comment: A Joint is an anatomical structure where two or more bones make contact, facilitating movement or providing stability. Also called articulation, bone joint, anatomical junction. Examples: knee joint, elbow joint, hip joint, shoulder joint. Distinct from Bone, which is a single skeletal component.

candidates.label: Characteristic
candidates.comment: A distinguishing quality or feature of something.

candidates.label: GatedResidenceCommunity
candidates.comment: A GatedResidenceCommunity is a Residence type that is a residential area with restricted access. Also called gated community, private estate. Examples: A luxury residential complex with controlled entry, a retirement community with security gates, a private housing development.

candidates.label: Month
candidates.comment: One of the twelve divisions of a year.

candidates.label: Heatwave
candidates.comment: A prolonged period of abnormally hot weather.

candidates.label: DrowningDeathEvent
candidates.comment: An event where a death occurs due to drowning.

candidates.label: ExcessDeathsEvent
candidates.comment: An event characterized by a higher-than-expected number of deaths in a given period.

candidates.label: Phenomenon
candidates.comment: A fact or situation that is observed to exist or happen.

candidates.label: Archipelago
candidates.comment: A group or chain of islands.

types.embedding_query_text: Signage: Signs, especially commercial or public signs. Also called Sign, Notice, Billboard. Examples: large sign.

chosen_type.label: Signage
chosen_type.definition: Signs, especially commercial or public signs, used for information or advertisement.
chosen_type.justification: No existing type directly captures the general concept of signage. 'CreativeWork' is the most appropriate parent as signs are created works.

candidates.label: Poster
candidates.comment: A Poster is a CreativeWork, typically a large, illustrated placard or announcement posted to advertise or publicize something. Also called placard, bill, advertisement. Examples: a movie poster, a concert poster, a political campaign poster, a scientific research poster.

candidates.label: SpecialAnnouncement
candidates.comment: A date-stamped textual information update from a locally-oriented organization, often related to urgent crisis situations, including contextual web links and structured data. Also called public notice, crisis update, community alert, emergency announcement. Examples: a school closure announcement due to weather, a pharmacy's updated operating hours during a pandemic, a local government's public health advisory.

candidates.label: PublicToilet
candidates.comment: A PublicToilet is a CivicStructure containing one or more toilets available for use by the general public, customers, or employees. Also called public restroom, public convenience, washroom. Examples: a toilet in a park, a restroom in a shopping mall, a public toilet facility at a train station, a highway rest stop bathroom.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

candidates.label: GovernmentPermit
candidates.comment: A GovernmentPermit is a formal authorization issued by a government agency. Also called public license, state approval, official authorization. Examples: building permit, driver's license, business operating license, fishing permit.

candidates.label: BusinessEvent
candidates.comment: A BusinessEvent is an Event related to commercial activities, such as conferences, trade shows, or corporate meetings. Also called corporate event, professional gathering, industry event. Examples: a sales conference, a product launch event, an annual shareholder meeting. Distinct from SocialEvent, which is for personal or recreational gatherings.

candidates.label: Characteristic
candidates.comment: A distinguishing quality or feature of something.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: PostalAddress
candidates.comment: A PostalAddress is a ContactPoint representing a mailing address. Also called mailing address, physical address, street address. Examples: 1600 Pennsylvania Ave NW, Washington, DC 20500; PO Box 123, Anytown, USA; a business's street address.

candidates.label: MedicalSign
candidates.comment: A medical sign or symptom that is an objective physical manifestation of a medical condition, discoverable by diagnostic tests or physical examination. Also called objective symptom, clinical sign, diagnostic finding. Examples: "fever", "rash", "high blood pressure", "swelling". Distinct from MedicalSymptom, which is subjective and reported by the patient.

types.embedding_query_text: Label: A small piece of paper, fabric, plastic, or similar material attached to an object and giving information about it. Also called Tag, Sticker, Mark. Examples: cryptic labels, GP, garden party.

chosen_type.label: Label
chosen_type.definition: A small piece of material attached to an object and giving information about it.
chosen_type.justification: No existing type directly captures the concept of a physical label. 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: BookmarkAction
candidates.comment: A BookmarkAction is an OrganizeAction where an agent marks an object for later retrieval or reference. Also called flag action, tag action, label action, mark action. Examples: saving a webpage to favorites, tagging an email, marking a chapter in an e-book.

candidates.label: MediaEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration providing codes and labels useful for describing media objects. Also called media classification, media type list, content category. Examples: "Video", "Audio", "Image", "Text".

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: Brand
candidates.comment: A Brand is an Intangible entity representing a name, symbol, or design used by an organization to identify and distinguish its products or services. Also called product line, trademark, label, marque. Examples: Nike, Apple, Coca-Cola, Google.

candidates.label: ReturnLabelSourceEnumeration
candidates.comment: ReturnLabelSourceEnumeration is an Enumeration listing several types of return labels for product returns. Also called return shipping label source, label provision method. Examples: InStore, PrintAtHome, ProductReturnService, DownloadAndPrint.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: DefinedTerm
candidates.comment: An intangible entity representing a word, phrase, or acronym with a formal definition, often used in glossaries or classification schemes. Also called Glossary entry, vocabulary term, classification code, concept. Examples: "ISBN" (International Standard Book Number), "HTTP" (Hypertext Transfer Protocol), "Organic" (as a food label). Distinct from DefinedTermSet, which is a collection of such terms.

candidates.label: MedicalDevice
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any object used in a medical capacity for diagnosing or treating a patient. Also called medical instrument, healthcare apparatus, diagnostic tool. Examples: a stethoscope, an MRI machine, a surgical scalpel, a blood pressure monitor.

candidates.label: Poster
candidates.comment: A Poster is a CreativeWork, typically a large, illustrated placard or announcement posted to advertise or publicize something. Also called placard, bill, advertisement. Examples: a movie poster, a concert poster, a political campaign poster, a scientific research poster.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Object' is the most generic entity, directly matching schema.org/Thing.

Examples: a screwdriver, a mixing bowl, a hammer, a computer. Distinct from HowToSupply, which is consumed during the process.

candidates.label: UseAction

Distinct from Thing, which is the root of all types, and CreativeWork, which is a specific type of intangible.

candidates.label: Vehicle

candidates.label: FireStation
candidates.comment: A FireStation is a CivicStructure housing firemen and fire-fighting equipment. Also called fire department, firehouse. Examples: The local city fire station, a volunteer fire department, a regional fire and rescue service.

types.embedding_query_text: Prop: An object used on stage or screen by actors during a performance. Also called Stage prop, Accessory, Item. Examples: large white staircase prop, large mirror ball.

chosen_type.label: Prop
chosen_type.definition: An object used on stage or screen by actors during a performance.
chosen_type.justification: No existing type directly captures the concept of a theatrical prop. 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

candidates.label: PerformAction
candidates.comment: A PerformAction, as a PlayAction, is the act of participating in performance arts. Also called act, perform, stage. Examples: performing in a play, playing a musical instrument on stage, dancing in a ballet. Distinct from PlayAction, which is a broader category for engaging in recreational activities.

candidates.label: Play
candidates.comment: A Play is a CreativeWork in the form of literature, primarily consisting of dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance. Also called stage play, drama, theatrical work. Examples: "Hamlet", "Death of a Salesman", "Hamilton", "A Streetcar Named Desire". Distinct from TheaterEvent, which is the actual performance of a play.

candidates.label: PerformingArtsEvent
candidates.comment: A PerformingArtsEvent is an event featuring live performances of arts like music, theatre, dance, or acrobatics. Also called live performance, show, stage event. Examples: a Broadway play, a ballet performance, a circus show, a stand-up comedy act. Distinct from MusicEvent, which is specifically for music.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: VideoObject
candidates.comment: A media object representing a video file. Also called video file, digital video, movie clip. Examples: an MP4 video, a YouTube video, a short film.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

Examples: a screwdriver, a mixing bowl, a hammer, a computer. Distinct from HowToSupply, which is consumed during the process.

types.embedding_query_text: Decoration: Something used to make a place or thing look more attractive. Also called Ornament, Embellishment, Adornment. Examples: red carpet, floral arrangements.

chosen_type.definition: Something used to make a place or thing look more attractive.
chosen_type.justification: No existing type directly captures the general concept of a decoration. 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: WearAction
candidates.comment: The act of dressing oneself in clothing or accessories. Also called put on, don, attire oneself. Examples: wearing a coat, putting on shoes, wearing a hat.

candidates.label: Poster

candidates.label: ArtGallery
candidates.comment: An ArtGallery is an EntertainmentBusiness that displays and often sells works of art. Also called gallery, art exhibition space, fine art dealer. Examples: The Louvre, a local contemporary art gallery, a commercial art dealership, a pop-up exhibition space.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: Florist
candidates.comment: A Florist is a Store that sells flowers and floral arrangements. Also called flower shop, floral designer. Examples: A local flower shop, an online florist delivering bouquets, a wedding floral specialist.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: Impact
candidates.comment: The effect or influence of one thing on another.

types.embedding_query_text: BuildingDescription: A textual characterization of a building's appearance or form. Also called Architectural description, Building characteristic. Examples: black puck of a building.

chosen_type.label: BuildingDescription
chosen_type.definition: A textual characterization of a building's appearance or form.
chosen_type.justification: No existing type directly captures the concept of a building description. 'CreativeWork' is the most appropriate parent as it is a created textual work.

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

candidates.label: Characteristic
candidates.comment: A distinguishing quality or feature of something.

candidates.label: Property
candidates.comment: A Property is an Intangible used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing, equivalent to rdf:Property. Also called attribute, characteristic, relation. Examples: "name", "description", "url", "author".

candidates.label: QualitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QualitativeValue is an Enumeration representing a predefined, non-numeric value for a product characteristic. Also called categorical value, descriptive value. Examples: garment size 'S', power cord plug type 'US', color 'red', material 'cotton'. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which represents a numerical point or interval.

candidates.label: FloorPlan
candidates.comment: A FloorPlan is an Intangible representing an explicit description of a collection of similar accommodations, providing common information like room counts, sizes, and layout diagrams. Also called layout plan, apartment layout, property blueprint. Examples: A floor plan for a two-bedroom apartment, a diagram showing the layout of an office suite, a blueprint for a house model.

candidates.label: SuperficialAnatomy
candidates.comment: Anatomical features observable by sight without dissection, including body form, proportions, and surface landmarks corresponding to deeper structures. Also called surface anatomy, external anatomy, visible body structures. Examples: the visible edges of the scapula, the cubital fossa for vein location, the contours of muscles under the skin.

candidates.label: TextDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A digital document primarily composed of textual content. Also called text file, digital document, e-document. Examples: a PDF report, a Word document, an e-book. Distinct from TextObject, which is a media object representing a text file, often for embedding or linking.

candidates.label: Room
candidates.comment: A distinguishable space within a structure, typically separated by interior walls. Also called chamber, compartment, space, area. Examples: a hotel room, a living room, a bedroom, a conference room.

candidates.label: MeasurementTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common types or dimensions of measurements. Also called dimension type, measurement category, sizing parameter. Examples: "chest circumference", "inseam length", "screw gauge", "wheel diameter".

candidates.label: BusinessEntityType
candidates.comment: A BusinessEntityType is an Enumeration representing the legal form, size, main line of business, or position in the value chain of an organization or business person. Also called legal entity type, company structure, business classification. Examples: Corporation, Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Non-profit Organization.

types.embedding_query_text: LocationType: A classification for a kind of place or area. Also called Place Category, Area Type. Examples: transit hub.

chosen_type.label: Class
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'LocationType' is a classification or category, which directly matches schema.org/Class.

candidates.label: Place

candidates.label: MapCategoryType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of different categories or kinds of maps. Also called map type, map classification, cartography category. Examples: "RoadMap", "SatelliteMap", "TerrainMap", "HybridMap".

candidates.label: GeoShape
candidates.comment: A GeoShape is a StructuredValue representing the geographic shape of a place, described using latitude/longitude pairs. Also called geographic area, spatial boundary, region. Examples: A polygon defining a city boundary, a circle representing a search radius, a line segment for a road.

candidates.label: Landform
candidates.comment: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

candidates.label: GeoCoordinates
candidates.comment: GeoCoordinates is a StructuredValue representing the geographic coordinates of a place or event, typically latitude and longitude. Also called geographic location, GPS coordinates, spatial coordinates. Examples: Latitude 34.0522, Longitude -118.2437 (for Los Angeles), a specific point on a map, the coordinates of an event venue.

candidates.label: GeoCircle
candidates.comment: A GeoCircle is a GeoShape representing a circular geographic area, defined by a center point and a radius. Also called circular region, geographic circle. Examples: A 5-mile radius around a city center, a circular search area defined by latitude/longitude and radius, a geofence for a specific location.

candidates.label: DataType
candidates.comment: DataType is a fundamental classification for the kind of values that can be stored or manipulated, such as numbers, text, or booleans. Also called primitive type, data format, value type. Examples: Integer, String, Boolean, Float, Date.

candidates.label: BusStop
candidates.comment: A BusStop is a CivicStructure designated as a place where buses regularly pick up and drop off passengers. Also called bus halt, bus stand, transit stop. Examples: a street corner bus stop, a designated stop on a campus route. Distinct from BusStation, which is a larger terminal facility.

candidates.label: BusinessEntityType
candidates.comment: A BusinessEntityType is an Enumeration representing the legal form, size, main line of business, or position in the value chain of an organization or business person. Also called legal entity type, company structure, business classification. Examples: Corporation, Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Non-profit Organization.

types.embedding_query_text: VenueType Examples: sports venue.

chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'VenueType' is a classification or category, which directly matches schema.org/Class.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: EventVenue
candidates.comment: An EventVenue is a CivicStructure that serves as a location for events. Also called venue, event space, performance hall. Examples: A concert hall, a stadium, a conference center, a community hall.

candidates.label: TennisComplex
candidates.comment: A local business or sports activity location featuring multiple tennis courts and related facilities. Also called tennis center, tennis club, tennis facility. Examples: 'Indian Wells Tennis Garden', a community tennis complex, a private tennis club.

candidates.label: SportsClub
candidates.comment: A local business or organization dedicated to a specific sport or range of sports, often offering membership and facilities. Also called athletic club, sports association, fitness club. Examples: a local tennis club, a community soccer club, a professional golf club.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: NightClub
candidates.comment: A NightClub is a local business that operates as a venue for dancing, entertainment, and socializing, typically at night. Also called discotheque, club, dance club. Examples: a popular city nightclub, a themed dance club, a music venue with late-night hours. Distinct from Bar, which may not feature dancing or a DJ.

candidates.label: Place

candidates.label: BowlingAlley
candidates.comment: A BowlingAlley is a SportsActivityLocation where people can engage in the sport of bowling. Also called bowling center, bowling lane, ten-pin alley. Examples: AMF Bowling, local bowling alley, a bowling club.

candidates.label: PerformingArtsTheater
candidates.comment: A PerformingArtsTheater is a civic structure or venue for performing arts. Also called theater, playhouse, concert hall. Examples: Sydney Opera House, a local community theater, a Broadway theater. Distinct from MovieTheater, which is for film screenings.

types.embedding_query_text: BuildingPart: A component or section of a building. Also called Architectural element, Structural component. Examples: floors.

chosen_type.label: BuildingPart
chosen_type.definition: A component or section of a building.
chosen_type.justification: No existing type directly captures the general concept of a building part. 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: WebPageElement
candidates.comment: A distinct part or component within a web page. Also called page component, web element, UI element. Examples: a navigation menu, an image, a form, a table.

candidates.label: HowToItem

candidates.label: AnatomicalStructure
candidates.comment: An AnatomicalStructure is a MedicalEntity representing any part of the human body, such as organs, tissues, or cells. Also called body part, biological structure, anatomical component. Examples: The heart, a bone, a muscle, a neuron, the liver. Distinct from AnatomicalSystem, which is a group of structures working together.

candidates.label: Room
candidates.comment: A distinguishable space within a structure, typically separated by interior walls. Also called chamber, compartment, space, area. Examples: a hotel room, a living room, a bedroom, a conference room.

candidates.label: GovernmentBuilding
candidates.comment: A GovernmentBuilding is a civic structure that houses government operations or services. Also called public building, state edifice, official premises. Examples: city hall, parliament building, courthouse, post office. Distinct from GovernmentOffice, which is a specific type of organization within a government building.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

candidates.label: Apartment
candidates.comment: An Apartment is a self-contained housing unit, a type of residential real estate that occupies only part of a building. Also called flat, condo, dwelling unit, residential unit. Examples: a studio apartment, a two-bedroom flat, a penthouse suite, a loft. Distinct from ApartmentComplex, which is a building containing multiple apartments.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
candidates.comment: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings is a place representing an important historical landmark or building. Also called historical site, heritage building, monument. Examples: Eiffel Tower, Colosseum, Statue of Liberty, a historic courthouse.

types.embedding_query_text: Substance: A particular kind of matter with uniform properties. Also called Material, Matter, Chemical. Examples: sweat.

chosen_type.label: Substance
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Substance' directly matches schema.org/Substance, representing any matter of defined composition.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: ChemicalSubstance
candidates.comment: A portion of matter with constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same or different types. Also called chemical compound, chemical, substance, molecule. Examples: Water (H2O), Sodium Chloride (NaCl), Ethanol, Oxygen.

candidates.label: BioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A fundamental Thing representing any biological, chemical, or biochemical substance or entity. Also called biochemical, chemical compound, biological entity, molecule. Examples: "A protein molecule", "A specific gene sequence", "A synthetic chemical compound", "DNA".

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: MolecularEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical entity representing any constitutionally or isotopically distinct atom, molecule, ion, or complex identifiable as a separate entity. Also called chemical entity, molecule, ion, compound. Examples: "water (H2O)", "glucose", "sodium ion (Na+)", "DNA". Distinct from BioChemEntity, which is a broader category for biological and chemical entities.

candidates.label: Drug
candidates.comment: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.

candidates.label: Intangible
candidates.comment: Intangible is a utility class serving as an umbrella for things that lack physical form, such as quantities, structured values, and concepts. Also called abstract entity, non-physical item, conceptual object. Examples: a number, a permit, a service, a list. Distinct from Thing, which is the root of all types, and CreativeWork, which is a specific type of intangible.

candidates.label: Property
candidates.comment: A Property is an Intangible used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing, equivalent to rdf:Property. Also called attribute, characteristic, relation. Examples: "name", "description", "url", "author".

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

types.embedding_query_text: Beverage: A drink, especially one other than water. Also called Drink, Liquid refreshment. Examples: beer.

chosen_type.label: MenuItem
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/MenuItem explicitly includes 'beverage' in its 'Also called' list and represents a single food or drink item.

candidates.label: DrinkAction
candidates.comment: DrinkAction is a ConsumeAction representing the act of swallowing liquids. Also called imbibing, sipping, quaffing. Examples: Drinking water, sipping coffee, consuming a soft drink, taking a shot of medicine.

candidates.label: LiquorStore
candidates.comment: A LiquorStore is a local business that sells alcoholic beverages such as wine, beer, and spirits. Also called off-license, bottle shop, wine shop, spirits retailer. Examples: a local wine and spirits shop, a beer distributor, a duty-free liquor store.

candidates.label: Distillery
candidates.comment: A Distillery is a FoodEstablishment that produces alcoholic beverages through distillation. Also called liquor producer, spirits manufacturer, alcohol plant. Examples: Jack Daniel's Distillery, The Macallan Distillery, Absolut Vodka Distillery. Distinct from Brewery, which produces beer through fermentation.

candidates.label: Brewery
candidates.comment: A Brewery is a FoodEstablishment that produces beer. Also called beer factory, microbrewery, brewpub. Examples: Guinness Brewery, Sierra Nevada Brewing Co., local craft brewery.

candidates.label: MenuItem
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a single food or drink item listed within a menu or menu section. Also called menu item, dish, beverage. Examples: "Spaghetti Carbonara", "Caesar Salad", "Coca-Cola", "Chocolate Lava Cake". Distinct from Menu, which is the entire list.

candidates.label: BarOrPub
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishment that primarily serves alcoholic beverages and often food. Also called bar, pub, tavern, lounge. Examples: "The Green Dragon Pub", "O'Malley's Bar & Grill", "The Corner Taproom". Distinct from Restaurant, which primarily focuses on serving meals.

candidates.label: Restaurant
candidates.comment: A Restaurant is a FoodEstablishment and LocalBusiness serving food and drink. Also called eatery, diner, cafe. Examples: "The French Laundry", a local pizzeria, a fast-food restaurant, a fine dining establishment.

candidates.label: Menu
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a structured representation of food or drink items available from a food establishment. Also called restaurant menu, food list, beverage list. Examples: a dinner menu, a wine list, a dessert menu, a cafe menu.

candidates.label: CafeOrCoffeeShop
candidates.comment: A CafeOrCoffeeShop is a FoodEstablishment primarily serving coffee, other beverages, and often light meals or pastries. Also called coffee house, coffee bar, cafe. Examples: Starbucks, local independent coffee shop, a small bistro. Distinct from Restaurant, which typically offers a wider range of full meals.

candidates.label: FoodEvent
candidates.comment: A FoodEvent is an Event centered around food and drink. Also called culinary event, gastronomic event, food festival. Examples: A wine tasting, a cooking class, a food fair, a restaurant week promotion.

types.embedding_query_text: Career: An occupation undertaken for a significant period of a person's life and with opportunities for progress. Also called Profession, Vocation, Employment. Examples: music career.

chosen_type.label: Occupation
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/Occupation explicitly includes 'career' in its 'Also called' list and fits the definition of a job or profession.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

candidates.label: WorkBasedProgram
candidates.comment: An educational and employment program structured around work-based learning, aiming to develop occupational competencies. Also called apprenticeship, vocational training, on-the-job training. Examples: an electrician apprenticeship, a culinary arts internship, a software development bootcamp with practical projects.

candidates.label: OccupationalExperienceRequirements
candidates.comment: OccupationalExperienceRequirements is an intangible entity indicating employment-related experience requirements. Also called job experience, work experience criteria, professional background. Examples: '5 years of experience in software development', 'entry-level position', 'management experience required'. Distinct from EducationalOccupationalCredential, which specifies formal qualifications.

candidates.label: EmploymentAgency
candidates.comment: An EmploymentAgency is a LocalBusiness that helps individuals find jobs and employers find suitable candidates. Also called recruitment agency, staffing firm, job placement service. Examples: A temporary staffing agency, an executive search firm, a headhunting company.

candidates.label: EmployeeRole
candidates.comment: An EmployeeRole is an OrganizationRole describing the relationship of an individual as an employee within an organization. Also called job position, staff role, employment status. Examples: "Software Engineer" at Google, "Marketing Manager" at a startup, "Cashier" at a supermarket.

candidates.label: JobPosting
candidates.comment: A JobPosting is an intangible listing that describes an open position within an organization. Also called job advertisement, employment listing, career opening. Examples: a software engineer job posting, a marketing manager vacancy, a retail associate opening.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: Characteristic
candidates.comment: A distinguishing quality or feature of something.

candidates.label: Standard
candidates.comment: A level of quality or attainment used as a benchmark.

types.embedding_query_text: Concept: An abstract idea or general notion. Also called Idea, Notion, Abstraction. Examples: privacy, imagine an artist so careful with imagery tying the knot inside.

chosen_type.label: Intangible
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/Intangible is a utility class for things that lack physical form, including concepts, which directly matches the OIE type 'Concept'.
