Distinct from Thing, which is the root of all types, and CreativeWork, which is a specific type of intangible.

candidates.label: MedicalIntangible
candidates.comment: A utility class under MedicalEntity for various intangible concepts in the medical space. Also called medical abstract, healthcare concept, clinical intangible. Examples: "MedicalConditionStage", "DoseSchedule", "MedicalCode". Distinct from MedicalEntity, which is the broader category for all medical things.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: CreativeWork
candidates.comment: A CreativeWork is the most generic type of intellectual or artistic creation, encompassing a wide range of media and forms. Also called artistic work, intellectual property, creation, content. Examples: A novel, a film, a photograph, a piece of software, a song, a painting.

candidates.label: DefinedTerm
candidates.comment: An intangible entity representing a word, phrase, or acronym with a formal definition, often used in glossaries or classification schemes. Also called Glossary entry, vocabulary term, classification code, concept. Examples: "ISBN" (International Standard Book Number), "HTTP" (Hypertext Transfer Protocol), "Organic" (as a food label). Distinct from DefinedTermSet, which is a collection of such terms.

candidates.label: MarryAction
candidates.comment: The act of entering into marriage with another person. Also called get married, wed, tie the knot. Examples: a wedding ceremony, a civil marriage, eloping.

candidates.label: Class
candidates.comment: An intangible concept representing a category or type of entity, equivalent to rdfs:Class. Also called type, category, kind, schema. Examples: "Person" class, "Product" class, "Event" class. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a specific term within a vocabulary.

candidates.label: Sculpture
candidates.comment: A three-dimensional work of art created by shaping or combining materials. Also called statue, carving, monument, artwork. Examples: Michelangelo's David, Rodin's The Thinker, a modern abstract metal sculpture, a clay bust.

candidates.label: ConstraintNode
candidates.comment: An intangible type supporting use cases where a node in a structured data graph describes properties that indicate sets of possible values rather than single, exact values. Also called constraint object, abstract node, descriptive node. Examples: A node describing a range of acceptable temperatures, a node specifying a set of required skills, a node defining a minimum and maximum quantity.

candidates.label: VisualArtwork
candidates.comment: A creative work that is primarily visual in nature, such as a painting, sculpture, or photograph. Also called art piece, visual art, artwork. Examples: Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa, a Rodin sculpture, an Ansel Adams photograph.

types.embedding_query_text: Role: The function assumed or part played by a person or thing in a particular situation. Also called Function, Capacity, Position. Examples: Collaborator, Tourist.

chosen_type.label: Role
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Role' directly matches schema.org/Role, which describes a function or part played by a person or thing.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: AssignAction
candidates.comment: An AssignAction is an AllocateAction representing the act of allocating an action, event, or task to a specific person or entity. Also called delegate, allocate, task, designate, appoint. Examples: assigning homework to students, delegating a task to an employee, assigning a case to a lawyer, designating a role in a project.

candidates.label: EmployeeRole
candidates.comment: An EmployeeRole is an OrganizationRole describing the relationship of an individual as an employee within an organization. Also called job position, staff role, employment status. Examples: "Software Engineer" at Google, "Marketing Manager" at a startup, "Cashier" at a supermarket.

candidates.label: UseAction
candidates.comment: The act of applying an object to its intended purpose or function. Also called utilize, employ, operate. Examples: using a tool to fix something, consuming food, wearing clothes.

candidates.label: AllocateAction
candidates.comment: AllocateAction, as an OrganizeAction, is the act of assigning resources to tasks, objects, or events. Also called assign, designate, distribute, earmark. Examples: Allocating budget to a project, assigning staff to a task, reserving a room for a meeting, distributing supplies.

candidates.label: CommunicateAction
candidates.comment: The act of transmitting information to another person or entity through a specific medium. Also called communication, conveying information, interacting. Examples: Sending an email, making a phone call, giving a speech, writing a letter. Distinct from InteractAction, which is a broader category of actions involving interaction.

candidates.label: Action
candidates.comment: An Action is a fundamental schema.org type representing an activity performed by an agent, potentially involving objects, participants, locations, and instruments, and producing a result. Also called activity, operation, deed, event. Examples: Reading a book, buying groceries, sending an email, cooking dinner.

types.embedding_query_text: FieldOfStudy: A branch of knowledge or academic discipline. Also called Discipline, Subject, Area of Study. Examples: Politics, Pop Culture.

chosen_type.label: Specialty
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/Specialty represents a branch of a field or academic discipline, fitting the OIE type 'FieldOfStudy'.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

candidates.label: MedicalStudy
candidates.comment: A medical entity that is an umbrella type covering all kinds of research studies relating to human medicine or health. Also called clinical study, health research, medical investigation. Examples: a drug trial, an epidemiological survey, a patient registry. Distinct from MedicalScholarlyArticle, which is the publication of study results, not the study itself.

candidates.label: MedicalStudyStatus
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing the status of a medical study. Also called study phase, research status, trial stage. Examples: "Recruiting", "Active, not recruiting", "Completed", "Terminated".

candidates.label: MedicalSpecialty
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing any specific branch of medical science or practice, including clinical and allied health specialties. Also called medical field, clinical discipline, healthcare area. Examples: "Cardiology", "Pediatrics", "Oncology", "Physical Therapy", "Dentistry".

candidates.label: MedicalObservationalStudyDesign
candidates.comment: An enumeration of design models for observational medical studies. Also called observational study type, research design, epidemiological design. Examples: "CohortStudy", "CaseControlStudy", "CrossSectionalStudy".

candidates.label: Researcher
candidates.comment: A Researcher is an Audience type representing individuals engaged in scientific or academic inquiry. Also called scientist, academic, scholar. Examples: a university professor, a lab scientist, a PhD student, an independent scholar.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

candidates.label: Course
candidates.comment: A Course is a description of an educational program or curriculum designed to impart knowledge, competence, or ability to learners. Also called educational program, curriculum, study program, academic course. Examples: "Introduction to Python Programming," "Art History 101," "Advanced Calculus," "Yoga Teacher Training." Distinct from CourseInstance, which is a specific offering of a course at a particular time and place.

candidates.label: ResearchProject
candidates.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

candidates.label: Thesis
candidates.comment: A scholarly document submitted by a candidate for an academic degree or professional qualification. Also called dissertation, academic paper, research thesis. Examples: a PhD dissertation, a master's thesis, an undergraduate honors thesis.

types.embedding_query_text: Activity: The state of being active or doing something. Also called Action, Task, Operation. Examples: use of phones, filming happening inside, guest arrivals, mid-afternoon cocktails.

chosen_type.label: Action
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Activity' directly matches schema.org/Action, representing an activity performed by an agent.

candidates.label: Action
candidates.comment: An Action is a fundamental schema.org type representing an activity performed by an agent, potentially involving objects, participants, locations, and instruments, and producing a result. Also called activity, operation, deed, event. Examples: Reading a book, buying groceries, sending an email, cooking dinner.

candidates.label: ActionStatusType
candidates.comment: ActionStatusType is an Enumeration representing the current state or status of an Action. Also called action state, status of action, progress status. Examples: `ActiveActionStatus`, `CompletedActionStatus`, `FailedActionStatus`, `PotentialActionStatus`.

candidates.label: ControlAction
candidates.comment: An action where an agent operates or manages a device or application. Also called controlling, operating, managing, manipulating. Examples: Turning on a light, adjusting a thermostat, launching a software application, steering a car. Distinct from Action, which is a general activity.

candidates.label: PlayAction
candidates.comment: PlayAction is an Action involving playing, exercising, training, or performing for enjoyment, leisure, recreation, competition, or physical activity. Also called performing, engaging in recreation, exercising. Examples: playing a sport, performing music on stage, training for a marathon, engaging in a hobby. Distinct from ListenAction, which is consuming music; Distinct from WatchAction, which is consuming visual content.

candidates.label: ConsumeAction
candidates.comment: The act of ingesting or utilizing information, resources, or food. Also called consumption, utilizing, ingesting, using. Examples: Reading a book, eating a meal, watching a movie, using electricity. Distinct from Action, which is a general activity.

candidates.label: ExerciseAction
candidates.comment: ExerciseAction is a PlayAction representing the act of participating in exertive activity to improve health and fitness. Also called working out, physical activity, training. Examples: Going for a run, lifting weights, practicing yoga, swimming laps.

candidates.label: ListenAction
candidates.comment: The act of consuming audio content, as a type of action. Also called hearing, audio consumption, listening activity. Examples: listening to music, hearing a podcast, attending an audio lecture.

candidates.label: OrganizeAction
candidates.comment: An OrganizeAction, as an Action, is the act of manipulating, administering, supervising, or controlling one or more objects. Also called arrange, manage, coordinate. Examples: organizing a conference, managing a project, arranging files on a computer. Distinct from CreateAction, which focuses on producing something new.

candidates.label: UserInteraction
candidates.comment: An outdated general type representing any interaction a user has with a web page or content. Also called user activity, user engagement, web interaction. Examples: a user clicking a link, submitting a form, scrolling a page.

candidates.label: FilmAction
candidates.comment: FilmAction is a CreateAction representing the act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally. Also called shooting a film, recording video, filming. Examples: Filming a movie scene, recording a documentary, shooting a wedding video, capturing a short clip on a phone.

types.embedding_query_text: LegalConcept: An idea or principle related to law or legal systems. Also called Legal principle, Jurisprudence concept. Examples: consent to video and photos.

chosen_type.label: LegalConcept
chosen_type.definition: An idea or principle related to law or legal systems.
chosen_type.justification: No existing type directly captures the general concept of a legal idea or principle. 'Intangible' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: AgreeAction
candidates.comment: AgreeAction, as a ReactAction, is the act of expressing a consistency of opinion with an object or proposition. Also called concur, assent, approve, consent. Examples: Agreeing with a statement, consenting to a proposal, approving a plan, liking a social media post. Distinct from DisagreeAction, which is the act of expressing an inconsistency of opinion.

candidates.label: LegalValueLevel
candidates.comment: LegalValueLevel is an enumeration of possible levels for the legal validity or authority of a legislation. Also called legislative authority level, legal hierarchy, law's binding power. Examples: 'Primary', 'Secondary', 'Tertiary', 'Advisory'.

candidates.label: LegalForceStatus
candidates.comment: LegalForceStatus is an enumeration of possible statuses for the legal force or validity of a legislation. Also called legal validity status, legislative effect, law status. Examples: 'InForce', 'Repealed', 'Expired', 'Pending'.

candidates.label: Legislation
candidates.comment: Legislation is a creative work representing a legal document such as an act, decree, or bill, or a component thereof. Also called law, statute, legal act, regulation. Examples: the Civil Rights Act, a local ordinance, a proposed bill in parliament. Distinct from LegislationObject, which is a specific file containing the legislation.

candidates.label: WatchAction
candidates.comment: The act of consuming dynamic or moving visual content. Also called view, observe, see. Examples: watching a movie, watching a live sports broadcast, watching a video tutorial.

candidates.label: PhotographAction
candidates.comment: A PhotographAction, as a CreateAction, is the act of capturing still images of objects using a camera. Also called taking a photo, shooting a picture, photography. Examples: taking a selfie, photographing a landscape, shooting a product for an advertisement. Distinct from RecordAction, which captures moving images or sound.

candidates.label: ViewAction
candidates.comment: The act of consuming or perceiving static visual content. Also called look at, observe, gaze upon. Examples: viewing a photograph, looking at a painting, examining a diagram.

candidates.label: FilmAction
candidates.comment: FilmAction is a CreateAction representing the act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally. Also called shooting a film, recording video, filming. Examples: Filming a movie scene, recording a documentary, shooting a wedding video, capturing a short clip on a phone.

candidates.label: LegalService
candidates.comment: A LegalService is a local business that provides legally-oriented services, advice, and representation. Also called law firm, legal practice, attorney service. Examples: a corporate law firm, a family law attorney, a public defender's office.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

types.embedding_query_text: Topic: The subject of a discourse, discussion, or artistic composition. Also called Subject, Theme, Matter. Examples: wedding chatter.

chosen_type.label: Topic
chosen_type.definition: The subject of a discourse, discussion, or artistic composition.
chosen_type.justification: No existing type directly captures the general concept of a topic or subject. 'Intangible' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: DiscussionForumPosting
candidates.comment: A social media posting that is an entry or message within an online discussion forum. Also called Forum post, message board entry, thread reply, online discussion. Examples: A question posted on a tech support forum, a comment in a gaming community thread, a new topic started on a hobby board. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically a longer, standalone article on a blog.

candidates.label: LiteraryEvent
candidates.comment: An event focused on literature, such as readings, book launches, or discussions. Also called book event, author appearance, literary gathering. Examples: a poetry reading, a book signing, a literary festival, a panel discussion with authors.

candidates.label: MarryAction
candidates.comment: The act of entering into marriage with another person. Also called get married, wed, tie the knot. Examples: a wedding ceremony, a civil marriage, eloping.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: ShortStory
candidates.comment: A brief work of literature, typically written in narrative prose, focusing on a single plot or theme. Also called tale, novelette, short fiction, narrative. Examples: Edgar Allan Poe's 'The Tell-Tale Heart', O. Henry's 'The Gift of the Magi', a story from a literary magazine.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: EventSeries
candidates.comment: An EventSeries is an Event representing a collection of events that share unifying characteristics, such as a recurring festival or a thematic lecture series. Also called event cycle, recurring event, series of events. Examples: The Olympic Games, a monthly book club meeting, a season of a concert series, a weekly farmers market.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

types.embedding_query_text: TimePeriod: A defined length of time. Also called Period, Era, Interval. Examples: holiday weekend.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'TimePeriod' directly matches schema.org/Duration, representing a defined length of time.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: DateRange
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a period of time defined by a start and end date.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: HolidayWeekend
candidates.comment: A weekend extended by a public holiday.

candidates.label: InstantaneousEvent
candidates.comment: An InstantaneousEvent is a structured value representing an event with no duration, such as a single point in time. Also called momentary event, point event, discrete occurrence. Examples: a computer log entry, a timestamp, a single click on a webpage. Distinct from Event, which typically has a duration.

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

types.embedding_query_text: Location: A particular place or position. Also called Place, Site, Spot. Examples: Manhattan's busiest corridor, Garden's loading bays.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Location' directly matches schema.org/Place, representing a particular place or position.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: Seat
candidates.comment: A specific seating location, often reserved, within an event venue or transportation. Also called reserved spot, seating assignment, chair, place. Examples: seat 12A on an airplane, row F seat 5 at a concert, a specific table at a restaurant.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: GeoCoordinates
candidates.comment: GeoCoordinates is a StructuredValue representing the geographic coordinates of a place or event, typically latitude and longitude. Also called geographic location, GPS coordinates, spatial coordinates. Examples: Latitude 34.0522, Longitude -118.2437 (for Los Angeles), a specific point on a map, the coordinates of an event venue.

candidates.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
candidates.comment: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings is a place representing an important historical landmark or building. Also called historical site, heritage building, monument. Examples: Eiffel Tower, Colosseum, Statue of Liberty, a historic courthouse.

candidates.label: Park
candidates.comment: A Park is a civic structure or area of natural, semi-natural, or planted space set aside for human recreation or protection of wildlife. Also called public park, green space, recreation area. Examples: Central Park in New York City, a local neighborhood park, a national park. Distinct from Garden, which is typically smaller and privately owned.

candidates.label: EventVenue
candidates.comment: An EventVenue is a CivicStructure that serves as a location for events. Also called venue, event space, performance hall. Examples: A concert hall, a stadium, a conference center, a community hall.

candidates.label: ShoppingCenter
candidates.comment: A large retail complex containing multiple stores and businesses, often with shared parking. Also called mall, shopping mall, retail complex, plaza. Examples: 'Westfield Century City', 'Mall of America', 'The Grove'.

candidates.label: VirtualLocation
candidates.comment: An online or non-physical location where events can be attended, such as a webinar or online meeting. Also called online venue, remote location, digital space. Examples: a Zoom meeting room, a webinar platform, a virtual conference hall.

types.embedding_query_text: AccessPoint: A place or means by which one can enter or exit. Also called Entry point, Exit point, Gateway. Examples: underground entry.

chosen_type.label: EntryPoint
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/EntryPoint explicitly includes 'access point' in its 'Also called' list and fits the definition of a place or means of entry/exit.

candidates.label: EntryPoint
candidates.comment: An EntryPoint is an Intangible representing a specific access point within a Web-based protocol. Also called API endpoint, access point, URL entry. Examples: A specific URL for an API call, a login page, a download link, a search form action URL.

candidates.label: ServiceChannel
candidates.comment: A specific means or method for accessing a service, such as a website, phone number, or physical office. Also called access point, service delivery method, contact channel, customer touchpoint. Examples: a company's customer service hotline, an online booking portal, a government agency's physical office, a mobile app.

candidates.label: SubwayStation
candidates.comment: A civic structure serving as a stop or terminal for subway or metro trains. Also called metro station, underground station, tube station. Examples: 'Grand Central Terminal', 'London Underground station', 'Tokyo Metro station'.

candidates.label: GatedResidenceCommunity
candidates.comment: A GatedResidenceCommunity is a Residence type that is a residential area with restricted access. Also called gated community, private estate. Examples: A luxury residential complex with controlled entry, a retirement community with security gates, a private housing development.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: ContactPointOption
candidates.comment: An enumerated option that describes a specific characteristic or service available at a ContactPoint. Also called contact option, communication preference, service feature. Examples: TollFree, HearingImpairedSupported, Available24Hours. Distinct from ContactPoint, which is the actual point of contact itself.

candidates.label: ContactPoint
candidates.comment: A specific point of contact for an organization or person, such as a customer service department. Also called contact information, communication channel, service point. Examples: A customer support phone number, an email address for sales, a physical address for returns, a social media handle. Distinct from ContactPointOption, which is an enumerated option related to a contact point.

candidates.label: DepartAction
candidates.comment: A move action representing the act of an agent leaving a specific location to travel towards a destination. Also called Leave, set off, embark, exit. Examples: A plane departing from an airport, a person leaving their home for work, a ship sailing from a port. Distinct from ArriveAction, which is the act of reaching a destination.

candidates.label: DataFeedItem
candidates.comment: A DataFeedItem is an individual entry or record contained within a larger DataFeed. Also called feed entry, feed item, data record. Examples: A single news article in an RSS feed, one product listing in an inventory feed, a single weather observation in a data stream.

candidates.label: Ticket
candidates.comment: An intangible item used to grant access or confirm a reservation for an event, travel, or service. Also called pass, voucher, entry permit. Examples: a concert ticket, an airline boarding pass, a bus ticket, a movie ticket.

types.embedding_query_text: EventType: A classification or category for a kind of event. Also called Event category, Type of occurrence. Examples: pre-party night, main ceremony, reception, wedding.

chosen_type.label: Class
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'EventType' is a classification or category, which directly matches schema.org/Class.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: EventSeries
candidates.comment: An EventSeries is an Event representing a collection of events that share unifying characteristics, such as a recurring festival or a thematic lecture series. Also called event cycle, recurring event, series of events. Examples: The Olympic Games, a monthly book club meeting, a season of a concert series, a weekly farmers market.

candidates.label: EventStatusType
candidates.comment: An EventStatusType is a StatusEnumeration whose instances represent various states an Event may be in. Also called event state, status of event. Examples: EventScheduled, EventCancelled, EventPostponed, EventRescheduled.

candidates.label: Class
candidates.comment: An intangible concept representing a category or type of entity, equivalent to rdfs:Class. Also called type, category, kind, schema. Examples: "Person" class, "Product" class, "Event" class. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a specific term within a vocabulary.

candidates.label: EventAttendanceModeEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EventAttendanceModeEnumeration is an Enumeration of modes for organizing an event, indicating whether it is online or offline. Also called attendance type, event format, participation mode. Examples: OnlineEventAttendanceMode, OfflineEventAttendanceMode, MixedEventAttendanceMode.

candidates.label: MapCategoryType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of different categories or kinds of maps. Also called map type, map classification, cartography category. Examples: "RoadMap", "SatelliteMap", "TerrainMap", "HybridMap".

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

candidates.label: ExhibitionEvent
candidates.comment: An ExhibitionEvent is an Event type focused on displaying items, such as at a museum, library, or tradeshow. Also called exhibit, show, display event. Examples: An art exhibition at a gallery, a historical display at a museum, a trade show for new technologies, a book fair.

candidates.label: EventVenue
candidates.comment: An EventVenue is a CivicStructure that serves as a location for events. Also called venue, event space, performance hall. Examples: A concert hall, a stadium, a conference center, a community hall.

candidates.label: DataType
candidates.comment: DataType is a fundamental classification for the kind of values that can be stored or manipulated, such as numbers, text, or booleans. Also called primitive type, data format, value type. Examples: Integer, String, Boolean, Float, Date.

types.embedding_query_text: Quality: A distinguishing characteristic or attribute. Also called Attribute, Characteristic, Property. Examples: not aesthetically pleasing.

chosen_type.label: Characteristic
chosen_type.definition: A distinguishing quality or feature of something.
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Quality' directly matches vocab/Characteristic, a distinguishing quality or feature.

candidates.label: Characteristic
candidates.comment: A distinguishing quality or feature of something.

candidates.label: Property
candidates.comment: A Property is an Intangible used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing, equivalent to rdf:Property. Also called attribute, characteristic, relation. Examples: "name", "description", "url", "author".

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

candidates.label: QualitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QualitativeValue is an Enumeration representing a predefined, non-numeric value for a product characteristic. Also called categorical value, descriptive value. Examples: garment size 'S', power cord plug type 'US', color 'red', material 'cotton'. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which represents a numerical point or interval.

candidates.label: Standard
candidates.comment: A level of quality or attainment used as a benchmark.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: BusinessAudience
candidates.comment: A BusinessAudience is an Audience defined by characteristics relevant to businesses, such as their industry, size, or role in the value chain. Also called B2B audience, corporate audience, professional audience. Examples: small business owners, IT managers, marketing executives, manufacturing companies. Distinct from PeopleAudience, which targets individual consumers.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

candidates.label: PropertyValueSpecification
candidates.comment: A PropertyValueSpecification is an Intangible defining the specification for a property's value. Also called value constraint, property definition. Examples: a specification for the allowed range of a numerical property, a definition of valid input for a text field, a schema for a complex property value.

types.embedding_query_text: Ability: The power or capacity to do or act. Also called Capability, Skill, Competence. Examples: make anything look pretty.

chosen_type.label: Ability
chosen_type.definition: The power or capacity to do or act.
chosen_type.justification: No existing type directly captures the abstract concept of an ability. 'Intangible' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: Course
candidates.comment: A Course is a description of an educational program or curriculum designed to impart knowledge, competence, or ability to learners. Also called educational program, curriculum, study program, academic course. Examples: "Introduction to Python Programming," "Art History 101," "Advanced Calculus," "Yoga Teacher Training." Distinct from CourseInstance, which is a specific offering of a course at a particular time and place.

candidates.label: PerformAction
candidates.comment: A PerformAction, as a PlayAction, is the act of participating in performance arts. Also called act, perform, stage. Examples: performing in a play, playing a musical instrument on stage, dancing in a ballet. Distinct from PlayAction, which is a broader category for engaging in recreational activities.

candidates.label: UseAction
candidates.comment: The act of applying an object to its intended purpose or function. Also called utilize, employ, operate. Examples: using a tool to fix something, consuming food, wearing clothes.

candidates.label: ViewAction
candidates.comment: The act of consuming or perceiving static visual content. Also called look at, observe, gaze upon. Examples: viewing a photograph, looking at a painting, examining a diagram.

candidates.label: WearAction
candidates.comment: The act of dressing oneself in clothing or accessories. Also called put on, don, attire oneself. Examples: wearing a coat, putting on shoes, wearing a hat.

candidates.label: OrganizeAction
candidates.comment: An OrganizeAction, as an Action, is the act of manipulating, administering, supervising, or controlling one or more objects. Also called arrange, manage, coordinate. Examples: organizing a conference, managing a project, arranging files on a computer. Distinct from CreateAction, which focuses on producing something new.

candidates.label: WatchAction
candidates.comment: The act of consuming dynamic or moving visual content. Also called view, observe, see. Examples: watching a movie, watching a live sports broadcast, watching a video tutorial.

candidates.label: WinAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving victory or success in a competitive activity. Also called triumph, succeed, prevail. Examples: winning a race, winning a championship, winning an argument.

candidates.label: AchieveAction
candidates.comment: AchieveAction is an instantaneous Action representing the accomplishment of something through prior efforts. Also called accomplish, attain, succeed, complete. Examples: Winning a race, graduating from college, reaching a sales target, completing a project.

types.embedding_query_text: Asset: A useful or valuable thing or person. Also called Resource, Advantage, Benefit. Examples: Swift's resources.

chosen_type.label: Resource
chosen_type.definition: A stock or supply of money, materials, staff, or other assets.
chosen_type.justification: vocab/Resource explicitly includes 'assets' in its definition, making it a suitable match for the OIE type 'Asset'.

candidates.label: Resource
candidates.comment: A stock or supply of money, materials, staff, or other assets.

candidates.label: FinancialIncentive
candidates.comment: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

candidates.label: UseAction
candidates.comment: The act of applying an object to its intended purpose or function. Also called utilize, employ, operate. Examples: using a tool to fix something, consuming food, wearing clothes.

candidates.label: Grant
candidates.comment: A Grant is an intangible, typically financial or quantifiable, allocation of resources from a funder to an organization or person, often supporting specific collective goals or projects. Also called funding award, financial aid, sponsorship, endowment. Examples: research grant, arts grant, student scholarship, disaster relief fund.

candidates.label: Property
candidates.comment: A Property is an Intangible used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing, equivalent to rdf:Property. Also called attribute, characteristic, relation. Examples: "name", "description", "url", "author".

candidates.label: TierBenefitEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific benefits offered as part of a loyalty or membership program. Also called loyalty program benefit, membership perk, reward tier. Examples: free shipping, early access to sales, exclusive content, dedicated customer support.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: FinancialProduct
candidates.comment: A FinancialProduct is a Service provided by financial institutions to consumers and businesses. Also called financial instrument, banking product, investment product. Examples: A savings account, a mortgage loan, an insurance policy, a mutual fund.

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

candidates.label: AllocateAction
candidates.comment: AllocateAction, as an OrganizeAction, is the act of assigning resources to tasks, objects, or events. Also called assign, designate, distribute, earmark. Examples: Allocating budget to a project, assigning staff to a task, reserving a room for a meeting, distributing supplies.

types.embedding_query_text: Experience: An event or occurrence that leaves an impression on someone. Also called Occurrence, Event, Encounter. Examples: amazing and irreplaceable experience.

chosen_type.label: Event
chosen_type.justification: An experience is an occurrence, which fits the general definition of schema.org/Event.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: EventSeries
candidates.comment: An EventSeries is an Event representing a collection of events that share unifying characteristics, such as a recurring festival or a thematic lecture series. Also called event cycle, recurring event, series of events. Examples: The Olympic Games, a monthly book club meeting, a season of a concert series, a weekly farmers market.

candidates.label: InstantaneousEvent
candidates.comment: An InstantaneousEvent is a structured value representing an event with no duration, such as a single point in time. Also called momentary event, point event, discrete occurrence. Examples: a computer log entry, a timestamp, a single click on a webpage. Distinct from Event, which typically has a duration.

candidates.label: EventStatusType
candidates.comment: An EventStatusType is a StatusEnumeration whose instances represent various states an Event may be in. Also called event state, status of event. Examples: EventScheduled, EventCancelled, EventPostponed, EventRescheduled.

candidates.label: Phenomenon
candidates.comment: A fact or situation that is observed to exist or happen.

candidates.label: EventReservation
candidates.comment: An EventReservation is a Reservation for an event like a concert, sporting event, or lecture. Also called ticket booking, event booking, seat reservation. Examples: A confirmed ticket for a concert, a reservation for a theater play, a booking for a conference session. Distinct from Offer, which describes the availability of tickets for sale.

candidates.label: EventVenue
candidates.comment: An EventVenue is a CivicStructure that serves as a location for events. Also called venue, event space, performance hall. Examples: A concert hall, a stadium, a conference center, a community hall.

candidates.label: ExhibitionEvent
candidates.comment: An ExhibitionEvent is an Event type focused on displaying items, such as at a museum, library, or tradeshow. Also called exhibit, show, display event. Examples: An art exhibition at a gallery, a historical display at a museum, a trade show for new technologies, a book fair.

candidates.label: LiteraryEvent
candidates.comment: An event focused on literature, such as readings, book launches, or discussions. Also called book event, author appearance, literary gathering. Examples: a poetry reading, a book signing, a literary festival, a panel discussion with authors.

candidates.label: VisualArtsEvent
candidates.comment: An event related to visual arts, such as an exhibition, gallery opening, or art fair. Also called art exhibition, gallery event, visual art show. Examples: a painting exhibition, a sculpture display, a photography festival.

types.embedding_query_text: Preference: A greater liking for one alternative over another or others. Also called Liking, Taste, Inclination. Examples: music taste.

chosen_type.label: Characteristic
chosen_type.definition: A distinguishing quality or feature of something.
chosen_type.justification: A preference is a distinguishing characteristic or attribute, fitting vocab/Characteristic.

candidates.label: ChooseAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a preference or making a selection from a set of options. Also called select, pick, opt for, decide. Examples: Choosing a meal from a menu, choosing a candidate in an election, choosing a color for a car.

candidates.label: UserLikes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of expressing approval or liking for content. Also called user like, content like, approval. Examples: a user liking a photo on social media, giving a thumbs-up to a video, favoriting an item.

candidates.label: LikeAction
candidates.comment: A LikeAction is a react action representing the act of expressing a positive sentiment about an object. Also called approve action, endorse action, favorite action. Examples: liking a post on social media, giving a thumbs-up to a video, expressing approval for an idea. Distinct from DislikeAction, which expresses negative sentiment.

candidates.label: VoteAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a preference or choice from a predefined set of options. Also called casting a vote, ballot, election. Examples: voting in a political election, casting a vote for a competition winner, participating in a poll.

candidates.label: EndorseAction
candidates.comment: EndorseAction is a ReactAction where an agent approves, certifies, likes, supports, or sanctions an object. Also called approve, support, certify, sanction. Examples: Liking a post on social media, certifying a product as organic, endorsing a political candidate, giving a positive review.

candidates.label: Impact
candidates.comment: The effect or influence of one thing on another.

candidates.label: ContactPointOption
candidates.comment: An enumerated option that describes a specific characteristic or service available at a ContactPoint. Also called contact option, communication preference, service feature. Examples: TollFree, HearingImpairedSupported, Available24Hours. Distinct from ContactPoint, which is the actual point of contact itself.

candidates.label: Characteristic
candidates.comment: A distinguishing quality or feature of something.

candidates.label: WantAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a desire or wish for an object or outcome. Also called desire, wish for, covet. Examples: wanting a new car, desiring a specific job, wishing for peace.

candidates.label: DislikeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative sentiment or disapproval towards an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express dislike, disapprove of, show aversion, downvote. Examples: Disliking a movie, expressing disapproval of a policy, downvoting a comment online. Distinct from LikeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or approval.

types.embedding_query_text: Opinion: A view or judgment formed about something, not necessarily based on fact or knowledge. Also called View, Belief, Stance. Examples: The right man for her is whoever she chooses.

chosen_type.label: Opinion
chosen_type.definition: A view or judgment formed about something, not necessarily based on fact or knowledge.
chosen_type.justification: No existing type directly captures the abstract concept of an opinion. 'Intangible' is the most appropriate parent.

mentions: The right man for her is whoever she chooses

candidates.label: AssessAction
candidates.comment: An AssessAction is an Action involving the formation of an opinion, reaction, or sentiment about something. Also called evaluate, appraise, judge, review, rate. Examples: a critic reviewing a movie, a teacher grading an assignment, a user rating a product, a doctor evaluating a patient's condition.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

candidates.label: OpinionNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An OpinionNewsArticle, as a NewsArticle, primarily expresses opinions rather than journalistic reporting of news and events. Also called opinion piece, editorial, column. Examples: an editorial in a newspaper, a political commentary, a personal essay in the opinion section. Distinct from Report, which presents factual findings.

candidates.label: DisagreeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative opinion or difference of opinion regarding an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express disagreement, object to, dispute, dissent. Examples: Disagreeing with a political statement, objecting to a proposed plan, disputing a fact. Distinct from AgreeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or agreement.

candidates.label: WatchAction
candidates.comment: The act of consuming dynamic or moving visual content. Also called view, observe, see. Examples: watching a movie, watching a live sports broadcast, watching a video tutorial.

candidates.label: ClaimReview
candidates.comment: A creative work that provides a fact-checking review of a specific claim. Also called fact-check, debunking, truth verification. Examples: A Snopes article debunking a viral claim, a PolitiFact rating of a politician's statement. Distinct from Review, which is a general assessment of an item.

candidates.label: AgreeAction
candidates.comment: AgreeAction, as a ReactAction, is the act of expressing a consistency of opinion with an object or proposition. Also called concur, assent, approve, consent. Examples: Agreeing with a statement, consenting to a proposal, approving a plan, liking a social media post. Distinct from DisagreeAction, which is the act of expressing an inconsistency of opinion.

candidates.label: ViewAction
candidates.comment: The act of consuming or perceiving static visual content. Also called look at, observe, gaze upon. Examples: viewing a photograph, looking at a painting, examining a diagram.

candidates.label: Claim
candidates.comment: A specific, factually-oriented statement that can be reviewed for accuracy. Also called assertion, statement, proposition, contention. Examples: "The Earth is flat," "Coffee cures cancer," "This product is 100% organic." Distinct from ClaimReview, which is the review of a claim.

candidates.label: Phenomenon
candidates.comment: A fact or situation that is observed to exist or happen.

types.embedding_query_text: MediaContent: Information or entertainment delivered through media channels. Also called Content, Media material, Broadcast. Examples: live feed.

chosen_type.label: WebContent
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/WebContent is a general type for any content accessible via the web, which fits 'MediaContent' like a 'live feed'.

candidates.label: BroadcastService
candidates.comment: A BroadcastService is a Service that delivers content via broadcast, either over the air or online. Also called broadcasting service, media transmission service, content delivery service. Examples: a national television network, a satellite radio provider, an internet radio service.

candidates.label: BroadcastEvent
candidates.comment: A BroadcastEvent is a PublicationEvent representing an event that is transmitted over the air or online. Also called live broadcast, streamed event, televised event, radio broadcast. Examples: a live news report, a sports game broadcast, a concert livestream.

candidates.label: BroadcastChannel
candidates.comment: A BroadcastChannel is an Intangible entity representing a specific instance of a BroadcastService within a cable or satellite lineup. Also called TV channel, radio station frequency, media channel. Examples: BBC One, CNN, ESPN, local public radio station.

candidates.label: RadioBroadcastService
candidates.comment: A RadioBroadcastService is a BroadcastService delivering radio content via broadcast over the air or online. Also called radio service, broadcast radio. Examples: BBC Radio 4, NPR, a local FM radio station, an internet radio stream.

candidates.label: CableOrSatelliteService
candidates.comment: A CableOrSatelliteService is a Service that provides access to media programming, such as TV or radio, delivered via cable or satellite infrastructure. Also called pay TV service, satellite radio provider, broadcast subscription service. Examples: Comcast Xfinity, DirecTV, SiriusXM Satellite Radio.

candidates.label: MediaSubscription
candidates.comment: An intangible service that grants a user access to media content, including audio, video, or books. Also called content subscription, media access plan, digital media membership. Examples: a streaming video subscription, an audiobook service membership, a digital newspaper subscription.

candidates.label: RadioSeries
candidates.comment: A RadioSeries is a CreativeWorkSeries dedicated to radio broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called radio show, radio program series. Examples: "The Archers", "This American Life", a long-running radio drama, a daily news radio program.

candidates.label: TelevisionChannel
candidates.comment: A unique instance of a television broadcast service on a cable or satellite lineup. Also called TV channel, broadcast channel, cable channel, satellite channel. Examples: 'HBO', 'CNN', 'BBC One', 'ESPN'.

candidates.label: WebContent
candidates.comment: A general type representing any content accessible via the web, including web pages, websites, and their elements. Also called web content item, online content, digital web asset. Examples: a blog post, an entire website, an image embedded on a page.

candidates.label: RadioSeason
candidates.comment: A RadioSeason is a CreativeWorkSeason dedicated to radio broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called radio series season. Examples: Season 1 of a radio drama, a specific year's collection of a weekly radio show, a themed season of a podcast broadcast on radio.
